title: [Henan University of Engineering x CLO] Only leaving one armhole dart, front piece dart transfer
description: This chapter will provide you with a detailed demonstration of the technique for transferring darts on the front piece, leaving only one armhole dart.
transcript:
Next, we will discuss how to perform the round-shaped processing on the front part of the round shape.  
We all know that there are more A, B, C, D, E, F components in the round shape,  
so it becomes more complicated when we actually manufacture it.  
Our A-shape and X-shape are all sawn.  
To simplify our production, we can combine all A-shape and B-shape components.  
In 3D, the round-shaped processing is relatively simple.  
We use the editor’s dot-and-line tool,  
press the Shift key to select the two edges of the A-shape,  
right-click and select Cut.  
At this point, we will cut this shape and delete it.  
After deleting it, press the Shift key to select the original shape edge of the A-shape,  
press the Shift key to select the original shape edge of the A-shape again,  
and press a button to merge it.  
In this way, we can see that the volume of the round shape will increase,  
and the volume will merge with the A-shape.  
Similarly, let us do the same for the B-shape.  
Press the Shift key to select the two edges of the A-shape,  
right-click, release the Shift key to select the A-shape,  
right-click again, and then select Cut.  
After cutting, you can delete this middle part,  
and after deleting it, switch to the edit and line tool,  
press the Shift key and then the left mouse button,  
and connect the two edges of the B-thread with the right-click.  
After we’ve done this,  
because the board is not symmetrical,  
we need to repeat the process.  
Now we have completed the process of removing the A-thread and moving it to the C-thread.  
We only need to keep the C-thread.

chunks.content: ## Overview of Round-Shaped Front Piece Processing This section explains the technique for simplifying the construction of a round-shaped front piece by consolidating multiple dart components (A, B, C, etc.) into fewer parts, specifically focusing on transferring dart volume to only one armhole dart. Key terms include dart transfer, A-shape, B-shape, C-shape, and 3D modeling tools. ## Simplification by Combining Dart Components Round-shaped garments typically include multiple dart components labeled A, B, C, D, E, and F, making manufacturing complex. To simplify, the process involves combining A-shape and B-shape components, effectively reducing the number of darts to manage. This consolidation reduces sewing complexity and streamlines production. ## Step-by-Step Dart Transfer Procedure Using a 3D Editor The process uses a 3D pattern editing tool with dot-and-line selection functions. The main operations involve cutting, deleting, and merging edges to transfer dart volume: 1. **Cutting the A-shape Dart** - Use Shift to select the two edges of the A-shape dart. - Right-click and select the Cut command to separate this dart segment. - Delete the cut A-shape segment. 2. **Merging Edges After Deletion** - Select the edges at the original location of the removed A-shape. - Use a merge function (activated by a specific button or command) to join these edges, effectively closing the gap. - This operation increases the overall volume of the front piece by merging with the adjacent dart C-shape. 3. **Repeating for the B-shape Dart** - Similarly, select the two edges of the B-shape dart with Shift, right-click and Cut. - Delete the middle B-shape part. - Using the dot-and-line edit tool, connect the two open edges of the B-thread by selecting them with Shift and left mouse click, then right-click to confirm the connection. 4. **Addressing Asymmetry** - Since the front board is not symmetrical, the same cutting, deletion, and merging steps must be repeated on the corresponding side to maintain garment balance. ## Outcome: Retaining Only One Armhole Dart (C-thread) After completing the cutting, deletion, and merging steps for both A-shape and B-shape darts, the front piece retains only the C-shape dart. This process effectively transfers dart volume from multiple darts into a single armhole dart, simplifying the garment’s construction while preserving the necessary shaping.
